Read Delphi ratings from a file

Source: R/read_delphi.R
read_delphi.Rd

Reads a CSV, TSV, TXT or Excel file of expert ratings and returns a validated delphi_data object. Three layouts are supported:

  • wide (layout = "wide", default): the DelphiR wide layout, with one row per expert and one column per item, as in the template created by delphi_template();

  • long (layout = "long"): one row per rating, with columns for the expert, the item and the rating, and optionally the round and the indicator; see delphi_data_long();

  • wide with two header rows (header_rows = 2): the layout produced by many survey platforms when each item is rated on several indicators. The first row gives the indicator of each column (for example impact, probability and desirability) and the second row the item statement, written once above the group of columns that refer to the same item (as with merged cells). Columns with an empty first-row cell, such as the expert identifier or demographic variables, are not treated as items.

Usage

read_delphi(
  file,
  ...,
  sheet = 1,
  layout = c("wide", "long"),
  header_rows = 1,
  items_sheet = NULL,
  indicator_names = NULL,
  item_prefix = "E",
  sep = NULL,
  dec = NULL,
  encoding = "UTF-8"
)

Arguments

file

Path to a .csv, .tsv, .txt, .xlsx or .xls file.

...

Arguments passed to delphi_data() (wide layout) or to delphi_data_long() (long layout), such as expert_col, round, indicator, scale and linked.

sheet

For Excel files, the sheet to read (name or position).

layout

"wide" (default) or "long"; see Description.

header_rows

Number of header rows of a wide file, 1 or 2; see Description.

items_sheet

For Excel files, an optional sheet with the item statements, in two columns named item and statement, as in the template created by delphi_template(). The statements are stored as item labels and used in reports.

indicator_names

For header_rows = 2, an optional named character vector that renames the indicators found in the first header row, for example c(IMPATTO = "impact", PROBAB = "probability"). The names used in scale must be the new ones.

item_prefix

For header_rows = 2, the prefix of the item codes. Items are coded in order of appearance (E1, E2, ...), and their statements are kept as item labels.

sep

Field separator for text files. By default it is detected from the first line: ";", "," or tab.

dec

Decimal mark for text files. By default "," when the separator is ";" (the usual European CSV export), "." otherwise.

encoding

File encoding for text files.

Value

A delphi_data object.

Details

Reading Excel files requires the readxl package. With one header row, column names are preserved exactly as they appear in the file, so that items may be coded E1, E2, ... or carry full labels. Rows without an expert identifier, such as summary rows with medians or quartiles added below the data, are ignored with a warning.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "delphi_round1.csv", package = "DelphiR")
x <- read_delphi(path, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact",
                 scale = c(1, 10))
x
#> <delphi_data>
#>   Experts:    15
#>   Rounds:     1 (1)
#>   Items:      8 (E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, ..., E8)
#>   Indicators: impact (from 1 to 10)
#>   Ratings:    119 (1 missing)
#> Use summary() for descriptive statistics.

# Two header rows: indicators in the first, item statements in the second
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c(
  ",Impact,Probability,Impact,Probability",
  "ID,Remote work becomes the norm,,AI agents manage recruitment,",
  "A,8,6,5,4",
  "B,9,7,6,6",
  "C,7,7,4,5"
), tmp)
y <- read_delphi(tmp, header_rows = 2, expert_col = "ID", scale = c(1, 10))
y
#> <delphi_data>
#>   Experts:    3
#>   Rounds:     1 (1)
#>   Items:      2 (E1, E2)
#>   Indicators: Impact (from 1 to 10), Probability (from 1 to 10)
#>   Ratings:    12 (0 missing)
#> Use summary() for descriptive statistics.
y$labels
#>                             E1                             E2 
#> "Remote work becomes the norm" "AI agents manage recruitment"
